rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete and material template. The child uses the same Buy American Act procurement framework, repeats its domestic-versus-foreign origin and price-differential machinery, and expressly identifies C01 by date and title while excluding petroleum from C01's general procedures. The child thus appears to be a petroleum-specific adaptation and partial displacement of C01. C06 supplied the immediate policy predicate but contains too little operative drafting to be the principal template. C12 shares contract-clause machinery, but only at a more generic level.

shared_material.child_excerpt: For the purposes of the application of the act of March 3, 1933 ... commonly known as the Buy American Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in the administration of the act of March 3, 1933 ... commonly known as the Buy-American Act
shared_material.explanation: Both directives organize their operative provisions around administration of the same procurement statute.

shared_material.child_excerpt: unless a domestic product is unavailable or its cost is determined to be unreasonable ... in considering bids no price differential will be applied between domestic and complying petroleum products
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the bid or offered price of materials of domestic origin shall be deemed to be unreasonable ... if ... [it] exceeds ... materials of foreign origin and a differential
shared_material.explanation: The child directly adapts C01's domestic-versus-foreign bid comparison and price-differential mechanism for petroleum purchases.

shared_material.child_excerpt: [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 17, 1954, "Prescribing Uniform Procedures for Certain Determinations under the Buy American Act," shall not be applicable to crude petroleum and petroleum products.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall apply only to contracts entered into after the date hereof.
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly identifies C01 and carves petroleum procurement out of its general procedures, demonstrating a direct legal and drafting relationship rather than mere topical similarity.
